handbookNote: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual, Version: March 2025 (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base manual, copyright 2022/2025 AAMVA, developed for State Driver License Agencies under FMCSA grant funding), published by the Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- fetched directly from https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/cdlhandbook.pdf on 2026-08-22 (confirmed reachable and downloaded without issue, unlike some other states' WAF-blocked domains; full text extracted via pdftotext to scratchpad/ks_cdl_research/ks_cdl_manual.txt, 9,581 lines) -- price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Real exam mechanics: unlike Idaho's 2022-edition manual, this Kansas manual edition does NOT contain an official 'Knowledge Test Information' table or any other passage stating exact question counts per knowledge test -- confirmed by exhaustively grepping the full extracted text for 'questions', 'passing score', 'number of questions', 'item bank', etc., all with zero hits. ksrevenue.gov's own CDL page (dovcdl.html) and CDL skills-testing-office page (dovcdltesting.html) were also checked directly and likewise state no item counts, no computer-based-testing details, and no third-party-tester specifics -- only that skills tests run 1-1.5 hours and are by appointment. Third-party test-prep sites (dmv-permit-test.com, cristcdl.com, etc.) commonly cite '50 questions / 40 correct' for the Kansas general knowledge test, but since that figure is NOT stated on any ksrevenue.gov or official Kansas manual page, it is deliberately NOT asserted anywhere in this question bank per this project's no-default-values discipline -- only the 80% minimum passing score, which IS federally standardized under 49 CFR 383.135(a) and therefore safe to assert regardless of item count, is used. Kansas's endorsement structure follows the standard federal six-endorsement AAMVA model exactly: H (Hazardous Materials, TSA background check required), N (Tank Vehicle, individual tank >119 gal / aggregate >=1,000 gal), P (Passenger, 16+ including driver), S (School Bus), T (Doubles/Triples), and X (combined Hazardous Materials + Tank Vehicle) -- no Kansas-specific extra endorsement letters or a separate non-CDL class exist in this manual, unlike Illinois's state-authored guide (Class D, Charter Bus C endorsement). Content-depth rationale: this is the generic AAMVA-authored 'Modernized Testing System' model manual (an older revision than Idaho's 2022 CDL Testing System edition, evidenced by mixed 'Version: July 2017' footers surviving on many interior pages alongside the March 2025 cover date, i.e. Kansas has adopted the modernized skills-test standard but kept the older knowledge-test narrative content largely intact) covering Section 1 Introduction (CDL Classes A/B/C, six endorsements, ten restriction codes, CLP rules and CLP-only endorsements, knowledge/skills test structure, medical certification/self-certification categories, inter/intrastate commerce status, disqualifications and out-of-service violations, other safety rules, International Registration Program), Section 2 Driving Safely (vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, shifting gears, seeing, communicating, controlling speed, managing space, seeing hazards, distracted/aggressive driving, night/fog/winter/hot-weather driving, railroad-highway crossings, mountain driving, driving emergencies, ABS, skids, accidents, fires, alcohol/drugs, fatigue, hazmat rules for all drivers), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (communication rules/shipping papers/placarding plus bulk packaging/loading/driving/emergency rules and glossary), Section 10 School Bus, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection Test, Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, and Section 13 On-Road Driving -- supporting a large, non-repetitive, well-grounded question pool of 576 questions before the build pipeline's automated dedupe pass. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Kansas manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers or item counts.
